articles.headline: GeneBench-Pro: OpenAI's protein-folding AI breaks new ground on molecular benchmarks
articles.body: OpenAI has released GeneBench-Pro, a specialized AI model designed to advance protein structure prediction and molecular biology research. The model demonstrates significant improvements on genetic and protein benchmarking tasks, outperforming previous baselines in accuracy and inference speed. GeneBench-Pro combines language model capabilities with domain-specific training on biological datasets, allowing it to reason about amino acid sequences, predict secondary and tertiary structures, and identify functional domains with higher precision than existing tools. The model has been evaluated against standard molecular biology benchmarks and shows measurable gains in metrics like RMSE (root mean square error) for structure prediction and accuracy on protein classification tasks. Unlike general-purpose AI models, GeneBench-Pro is optimized for the specific constraints of biological data—irregular sequences, limited training examples for rare proteins, and the need for physically plausible predictions. This positions it as a tool for computational biologists, pharmaceutical researchers, and biotech companies looking to accelerate drug discovery pipelines. The release includes API access and benchmark datasets, enabling researchers to reproduce results and build on the model's capabilities.

Feed multiple related sequences to identify conserved functional domains across protein families instantly.
Input a mutation and see predicted impact on protein folding stability compared to wild-type baseline.

articles.hook: Google just made building production AI agents way less painful.
articles.headline: Google Expands Gemini Managed Agents With Background Tasks and Remote MCP
articles.body: Google has announced new capabilities for Managed Agents in the Gemini API, giving developers tools to build production-ready autonomous agents more reliably. The update introduces background task execution and remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) support, allowing agents to perform long-running operations without blocking user interactions and to connect with external tools and data sources remotely. This addresses a major pain point in agent development: the need to integrate with existing systems while maintaining stability and responsiveness. Managed Agents abstract away the complexity of orchestrating multiple API calls, memory management, and tool invocation, letting developers focus on defining what tasks they want agents to accomplish. The background tasks feature enables agents to handle time-consuming operations like data processing, file generation, or API polling asynchronously. Remote MCP support extends the agent's capability to interact with external services and proprietary tools without requiring everything to run in the same environment. Before this announcement, developers building production agents faced challenges around handling concurrent requests, managing state across long operations, and integrating with diverse external systems. These new capabilities position Gemini Managed Agents as a more complete alternative to building custom agent orchestration from scratch, similar to what other platforms like Anthropic's Tools and OpenAI's Assistants API offer. The real-world impact is immediate: developers can now deploy agents that handle complex, multi-step workflows in production without the infrastructure headaches that typically come with autonomous systems.
examples: Schedule an agent to process customer support tickets overnight and summarize findings for the team by morning.
Connect an agent to your internal CRM, knowledge base, and payment system through remote MCP integrations.
Build a multi-step data analysis workflow where the agent queries, transforms, and generates reports asynchronously.
